Legacy power decomposition analysis (Acycle PDA menu / DYNOT core)

Source: R/pda_legacy.R
pda_legacy.Rd

The pda_legacy function reproduces the power decomposition analysis as run from the Acycle menu "Power Decomposition Analysis" and as used inside DYNOT (pdan.m; Li et al., 2016). Preprocessing as in the Acycle menu: rows with NA are removed, data are sorted, duplicated depths are replaced by their mean, unevenly sampled data (relative tolerance 1e-5) are linearly interpolated at the median sampling interval, and the series is optionally padded by half a window at both ends (zeropad2.m). In each window of trunc(window/dt) samples the data are linearly detrended and the adaptive MTM spectrum (pmtm(x, nw, pad)) is computed. Target and total powers are sums of spectral bins selected with the historical proportional bin mapping (lower = ceiling(nbin*f/fNyq), upper = trunc(nbin*f/fNyq)); overlapping target bands are counted once. Window centers are evenly spaced between first coordinate + window/2 and last coordinate - window/2. Translated from Acycle v3.1 pdan.m, zeropad2.m, interpolate.m, findduplicate.m and AC.m (menu_pda_Callback) (Mingsong Li).

Usage

pda_legacy(
  data = NULL,
  target_bands = c(1/45, 1/25),
  window = 500,
  nw = 2,
  f_min = 0,
  f_max = NULL,
  step = 1,
  pad = 5000,
  pad_type = 1,
  genplot = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Two-column numeric matrix or data frame: depth/time in column 1 and the proxy value in column 2 (further columns are ignored). Rows with NA are removed, the data are sorted, duplicated depths are averaged and unevenly sampled data are interpolated at the median sampling interval. Required (Default=NULL).

target_bands

Target frequency bands whose summed power is divided by the power of the total band, in cycles per unit of the depth/time column: a numeric vector of paired limits c(lower1, upper1, lower2, upper2, ...) (any order within a pair) or a B x 2 matrix with one band per row; overlapping bands are counted once. Default=c(1/45, 1/25).

window

Length of the moving window in the unit of the depth/time column (numeric, > 0); each window holds trunc(window / dt) samples. Default=500.

nw

Time-bandwidth product of the DPSS (Slepian) tapers of the multitaper spectrum (numeric, > 0); larger values smooth the spectrum more. Default=2.

f_min

Lower cutoff frequency of the total band, in cycles per unit of the depth/time column (numeric, >= 0). Default=0.

f_max

Upper cutoff frequency of the total band, in cycles per unit of the depth/time column (numeric, > f_min); values above the Nyquist frequency are clipped. NULL uses the Nyquist frequency. Default=NULL.

step

Step between successive windows, in number of samples (positive integer). Default=1.

pad

Length of the FFT used by the multitaper spectrum, i.e. the zero-padding number of pmtm (positive integer); larger values give a finer frequency grid. Default=5000.

pad_type

Padding of both ends of the (demeaned) series by half a window before the analysis, so that the windows cover the whole record (integer): 0 none, 1 zeros, 2 mirror image of the record, 3 mean of the first/last half window, 4 random values with the mean and standard deviation of the first/last half window. Default=1.

genplot

Plot the power ratio against depth/time (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

verbose

Show a progress bar over the windows (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A matrix with columns window center, ratio (target / total), target power and total power.

References

Li, M., Huang, C., Hinnov, L., Ogg, J., Chen, Z.-Q., Zhang, Y., 2016. Obliquity-forced climate during the Early Triassic hothouse in China. Geology 44, 623-626. doi:10.1130/G37970.1

Li, M., Hinnov, L., Kump, L., 2019. Acycle: Time-series analysis software for paleoclimate research and education. Computers & Geosciences 127, 12-22. doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2019.02.011

Author

Michiel Arts (R translation); original MATLAB code: Mingsong Li and Linda Hinnov (Acycle); zeropad2 padding options by Nicolas Thibault and Giovanni Rizzi.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
t <- seq(0, 2000, by = 2)
x <- sin(2 * pi * t / 40) + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * t / 100) +
  0.5 * as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.7), n = length(t)))
res <- pda_legacy(data = cbind(t, x), target_bands = c(1/45, 1/35),
  window = 300, step = 5, pad = 1000, pad_type = 1)
head(res)
#>      center     ratio target_power total_power
#> [1,]      0 0.3606305     24.11534    66.86996
#> [2,]     10 0.3589282     25.18059    70.15496
#> [3,]     20 0.3444931     25.51678    74.07050
#> [4,]     30 0.3392978     25.92545    76.40913
#> [5,]     40 0.3335794     26.36172    79.02684
#> [6,]     50 0.3324595     27.78380    83.57049
# }
